extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and KIPO staff (Korean patent practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and eligibility criteria under the Korean Patent Act for fee exemptions/reductions, refunds, document inspection/referencing, confidentiality/offences, and basic patent entitlement. Focused on what applicants/representatives must submit and when, who qualifies for relief, and administrative safeguards/penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-category full exemption eligibility and evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain socially disadvantaged categories may be exempt from patent/official fees (e.g., recipients under the National Basic Livelihood Security Act; persons of national merit and surviving/bereaved families; Agent Orange victims and related categories; registered disabled persons; students; persons in military or public service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only when the inventor and the applicant are identical (where specified). One copy of the concerned evidential documents must be submitted. The designation as a recipient/disabled/person of national merit/students/etc. must exist at the time of submission of documents such as a patent application; otherwise the exemption does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered partial exemption/reduction categories and percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent/application/examination/annual/utility-model fees may be reduced or exempted by specified percentages (examples in the text include exemptions/reductions by 85%, 70%, 50%, 30% depending on the subject of exemption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the manual: 85% exemption applies in certain cases (e.g., age bands such as younger than 30 but >=19, 65 years and over, inventor==applicant as listed); 70% reduction applies to individuals (only when inventor is the applicant) and to small enterprises meeting statutory criteria; 50% and 30% reductions apply to other categories such as joint research between conglomerates and SMEs, public research organizations, technology transfer task forces, mid-sized firms, and local governments. The manual provides detailed industry-by-industry revenue thresholds for classifying small/medium/medium-enterprises and enumerates required evidential documents (e.g., copy of business registration certificate, financial statements proving average sales/total assets for 3 business years). In calculating exemption amounts, amounts less than 100 won are not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enterprise classification and evidential-document requirements for reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Small/medium/medium-enterprise status (and industry classification) determines eligibility and percentage of fee reduction; evidential documents must be provided to prove enterprise category and financial thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual lists business-classification thresholds (e.g., businesses with average revenue less than specified won amounts per industry category: 12 billion, 8 billion, 5 billion, 3 billion, etc., and more detailed thresholds for medium enterprises such as 150 billion, 100 billion, 80 billion, 60 billion, 40 billion depending on industry). Required evidential documents include a copy of business registration certificate and documents proving SME status or total assets/average sales for 3 business years (e.g., financial statements). Some exemptions apply only in the case of employee inventions (design/creation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-applicant requirement for personal exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant files personally and wishes to obtain fee exemption/reduction, the applicant must be the inventor or designer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant who filed personally is not the inventor/designer, they are not eligible for the personal-exemption categories described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for requesting fee reduction/exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for fee reduction or exemption and the subject for reduction/exemption must be stated at the time of filing an application, making a request for examination, or submitting annual fee payment documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person fails to apply for reduction/exemption at the time of filing or requesting examination and later applies on the ground that they were entitled earlier, the later application for reduction/exemption shall not be recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding for reduction/exemption: submission and reuse of evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents supporting a claim for fee reduction/exemption must be submitted to the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office; previously submitted evidential documents may be referenced in subsequent proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidential documents for persons with national merit, registered handicapped persons, or recipients of National Basic Livelihood Security have already been submitted to the Commissioner, re-submission may be unnecessary. To skip re-submission, state the intention to skip and provide index information of the submitted documents. Referencing rules (see separate referencing criterion) explain how to indicate references in forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refundable fee situations (grounds for refund)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees or official fees are refundable upon request in specified situations such as fees paid by mistake, fees paid where an application is not accepted, fees for invalidated/abandoned applications, fees after a decision to revoke/invalidate a patent, and other enumerated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual enumerates many refund cases: (①) fees paid by mistake (including fees where an application is not accepted/returned; excess payments; fees in case of invalidation/disapproval); (②) patent fees for years after a decision to revoke a patent becomes final; (③) patent fees after invalidation of patent-term extension becomes final; (④) application and examination request fees where the application is invalidated or abandoned within one month of filing (for applications filed after July 1, 2007); (⑤) paid examination request fees where the requested examination was later withdrawn/abandoned before certain procedural stages (with conditions and exceptions); (⑥) patent fee for the following year after abandonment; (⑦)-(⑨) partial refunds of trial/trial-participation fees in circumstances of withdrawal or rejection before merits review closes. The manual gives specific procedural conditions for each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request a fee refund
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for refund of fees paid by mistake must be made by the person whose name is in the signature box on the receipt of fee payment or by a person with power of attorney; similar rules apply for refunds following revocation/invalidation decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an examiner intends to make a decision that would lead to a refund, the examiner must deliver a notice of invalidation with guidance on the refund proceeding to the payer. Registered patent right holders or persons with power of attorney can request refunds related to revocation/invalidation refunds as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of patent-related documents: who may request and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to obtain a certificate/certified copy/extract or to inspect/photocopy Patent Register entries or documents may file a request with the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the IP Trial & Appeal Board under Annexed Form No.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner/President may refuse inspection/copy where the document contains confidential information, including: (1) a patent application document that has not been laid open or registered (with specified exceptions for earlier priority applications that have been laid open/registered), (2) documents for an appeal trial to final rejection for an application not laid open/registered, (3) documents that may harm public health or contravene public order or morality. Also, documents relating to pending examinations/trials/retrials may be refused for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on taking out documents and giving opinions on pending cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents relating to patent applications, examinations, opposition proceedings, trials, retrials or the Patent Register may only be taken out under narrowly defined conditions; no opinion/testimony/answer may be given regarding pending cases or details of decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 217 allows taking out documents only for purposes such as prior-art searches under Article 58(1)/(2), digitization of patent documents, or online remote working under the Electronic Government Act. Paragraph (2) forbids giving opinions, testimony, or answers about pending applications, examinations, opposition proceedings, trials, retrials, or decisions on grant/refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offense of divulging confidential information and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any current or former employee of KIPO or the IP Trial & Appeal Board who divulges or misappropriates confidential information about an invention of a pending patent application (including pending international applications) acquired in the course of performing duties shall be subject to criminal penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty described: imprisonment for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 50 million won. The scope includes executives/employees of specialized agencies designated under Article 58(1) and agencies for digitization of patent documents (they are deemed public officials for this purpose). Definitions: 'divulgence' includes intentional and accidental informing of a third party; 'misappropriation' includes working the invention or filing an application on a subordinate/subservient invention related to the concerned invention against the right holder's intention. The manual explains the relation to other criminal provisions concerning public-official duties and related offences (e.g., violation of duties, abuse of power, bribery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing already-submitted evidential documents (document reuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person conducts more than two patent-related proceedings simultaneously or consecutively with the same evidential documents, the person may submit the original evidential documents for one proceeding and reference them in other proceedings by submitting copies or stating the intention to reference the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referencing can be made in many specific cases including: power of attorney for representative proceedings; evidential documents showing an invention has not been disclosed; priority-claim documents; evidential documents of a representative of more than two parties; evidential documents of a successor in title; documents where permission/approval/consent of a third party is needed; nationality/certificate documents for foreigners; documents relating to changes/corrections of name/domicile/seal. When copies are submitted instead of originals, the intention to reference must be stated in the attached-documents box in the form; an example format for the statement is provided in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority-of-representative evidential documents exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents proving a representative's authority need not be submitted in certain situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) where a representative who has made a notification of appointment under Article 5(2) of the Enforcement Rules conducts a proceeding within the power of attorney; (2) where a representative who has registered a general power of attorney under Article 5(2)(2) conducts proceedings within the scope of the general power of attorney; (3) where a representative conducts proceedings within the scope of the power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to a patent and protection against unentitled filers
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who makes an invention or his/her successor is entitled to a patent; joint inventors are jointly entitled. Employees of KIPO/IPTAB are not entitled to a patent while in office except by inheritance/bequest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent is refused because the filer is an 'unentitled person' (not the inventor or a successor), then a patent application filed by a legitimate right-holder subsequent to that application shall be deemed filed on the date of filing of the unentitled person's application, provided the legitimate right-holder files within 30 days after the rejection date. This protection applies subject to the conditions stated in Article 34.
